sections.label: CPIB corruption case dollar value
sections.summary: CPIB does not compute the aggregate dollar value of corruption cases prosecuted because corruption does not always involve money.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: CPIB does not compute the aggregate dollar value of corruption cases prosecuted as corruption does not always involve money.

sections.label: Forfeiture values and pandemic digitalisation
sections.summary: Forfeitures imposed by the Courts for CPIB cases in 2018, 2019 and 2020 were about $2.4 million, $3.8 million and $2.2 million respectively, and the pandemic underscored digital transformation's importance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: In 2018, 2019 and 2020, the total value of forfeitures imposed by the Courts for CPIB cases were about $2.4 million, $3.8 million and $2.2 million respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: The pandemic underscored the importance of digital transformation as some of CPIB's initiatives on this front had minimised disruption to its operations and service delivery.

sections.label: Command Centre and forensic analytics
sections.summary: Examples include a new Command Centre enhancing situational awareness and upgraded digital forensic analytics capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing) (for the Prime Minister)
sentences.text: Some examples include the setting up of a new Command Centre that enhances situational awareness and the upgrading of digital forensic analytics capabilities.

sections.label: PCA punishment and legislative review
sections.summary: Three areas: aligning PCA offence punishment with other economic crimes, comparative international legislation studies including separate punishment for corporate bodies, and reviewing expansion of extraterritorial provisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: First is to ensure that the punishment for PCA offences are in line with those of other economic crimes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Second, to conduct comparative studies on international legislation to assess, amongst other things, if there is a need to have separate punishment for corporate bodies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Third, to review the need to expand the current extraterritorial provisions by examining past cases where CPIB is not able to take action on foreigners performing outsourced law enforcement functions where the corrupt transactions were undertaken overseas.

sections.label: Business confidence in Singapore rules
sections.summary: Businesses must remain fully confident to invest in Singapore because rules and processes are fair, coherent and transparent, creating quality jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Ultimately, businesses must remain fully confident that they can plant their investments here in Singapore because our rules and processes are fair, coherent and transparent; thereby, creating quality jobs for fellow Singaporeans.
